column2: the planned dedup generalizes marker tokens, read fallback, and sidecars in `skills/shared/final-summary-emit.md`, but marker-first step 1 still hardcodes design-only `<task-notification>` stdout as the extraction source while `/implement` step 17 and step 18b extract from foreground captured bash wrapper stdout (`step-16-17` / `step-18.sh --phase finalize`). steps 5–6 still unconditionally mandate read fallback and `report_gate_sidecars_file` sidecar follow-on, which conflicts with implement’s no-read / no-sidecar path. restructuring around caller policies can also drop the existing no task-output re-read and in-context-only constraints (current steps 3–4), leaving dual or conflicting source rules and weakening the dedup.

the never #17 edit list requires the shared pointer, implement marker pair, and no-read fallback, but not that the source is captured foreground wrapper stdout (not `<task-notification>`). replacing inline extract-from-captured-wrapper-stdout text with a bare marker-first pointer can reintroduce the design-only notification source at the highest-priority rule operators read first.

generalizing marker-first step 1 without a normative design binding leaves six `/design` callsites that only say “follow marker-first profile” and name task-notification source without citing `larch_final_summary_begin` / `larch_final_summary_end`. today step 1 embeds design markers; replacing that with caller-supplied markers plus examples-only text unbinds `/design` unless every callsite is edited.

`skills/shared/final-summary-emit.md` line 17 still says "use this profile when a completed background task can emit markers." the dedup plan generalizes marker-first steps around caller-supplied sources but does not require updating that intro. after generalization, `/implement` step 17 and step 18b bind foreground captured bash wrapper stdout, not `<task-notification>` output. readers who stop at the profile header may treat marker-first as design-only and skip implement foreground extraction.

`skills/design/skill.md` line 29 anti-halt continuation references the shared final-summary emit contract via "marker-first profile for completed step 5c task output" but is omitted from the plan's enumerated binding-site list (final summary block, step 5c abort, step 5c item 5, step 5d). it lacks explicit `larch_final_summary_begin` / `larch_final_summary_end` tokens and a named notification stdout source binding. an implementer who edits only the four named sites leaves the highest-priority design rule unbound after shared step 1 is generalized, so operators may apply wrong markers, notification vs foreground semantics, or read fallback on step 5c handoff. the harness pin at `scripts/test-render-cost-line-callsites.sh:94` currently matches only this anti-halt substring for the `_publish_rc` carve-out, not operational step 5d or step 5c item-5 gates.

the plan replaces the anti-halt embedded sentence containing `marker-first profile for completed step 5c task output when _publish_rc is 0, 1, or 3` with a compact shared-profile pointer plus explicit binding pins, but only schedules new pins near line 94 and does not retire the existing line-94 grep that still requires that exact substring. after the skill edit, `make test-render-cost-line-callsites` fails at line 94 even when runtime behavior is correct.
